## Figure 1.7: Long-Term Net Transfers on External Debt in Low- and Middle-Income Countries, by Debtor Type, 2015–25
Line chart

- **Units:** US$ (billion)
- **X-axis:** Years, **2015–2025**
- **Y-axis:** US$ (billion), range **–200 to 400**
- **Series / legend:**
  - **Long-term + IMF** (dark blue)
  - **Private nonguaranteed** (orange)
  - **Public and publicly guaranteed + IMF** (light blue)
- **Geographic/group coverage:** Low- and middle-income countries
- **Reference line:** Dashed horizontal line at **0**

### Approximate values by series
Values are estimated from line positions unless directly stated in the text layer.

| Year | Long-term + IMF | Private nonguaranteed | Public and publicly guaranteed + IMF |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2015 | ≈90 | ≈25 | ≈70 |
| 2016 | ≈115 | ≈25 | ≈90 |
| 2017 | ≈290 | ≈125 | ≈165 |
| 2018 | ≈210 | ≈40 | ≈170 |
| 2019 | ≈130 | ≈35 | ≈90 |
| 2020 | ≈210 | ≈45 | ≈165 |
| 2021 | ≈185 | ≈10 | ≈170 |
| 2022 | ≈-175 | ≈-135 | ≈-40 |
| 2023 | ≈-190 | ≈-125 | ≈-60 |
| 2024 | ≈-120 | ≈-123 | ≈5 |
| 2025 | ≈50 | ≈0 | ≈50 |

### Rankings and comparisons
- **Highest value in the figure:** **Long-term + IMF** in **2017**, at approximately **$290 billion**.
- **Lowest value in the figure:** **Long-term + IMF** in **2023**, at approximately **–$190 billion**.
- In **2015–2021**, **Long-term + IMF** is generally the largest of the three series.
- **Public and publicly guaranteed + IMF** is consistently positive from **2015 to 2021**, turns negative in **2022–2023**, returns to slightly positive in **2024**, and rises further in **2025**.
- **Private nonguaranteed** is positive from **2015 to 2021**, negative in **2022–2024**, and returns to about **zero** in **2025**.
- In **2022**, all three series turn negative, with the sharpest drop in **Long-term + IMF**.
- In **2024**, **Public and publicly guaranteed + IMF** is the only series slightly above zero.
- In **2025**, **Long-term + IMF** and **Public and publicly guaranteed + IMF** are both around **$50 billion**, while **Private nonguaranteed** is around **0**.

### Trends
- **Long-term + IMF:** Rises from 2015 to a peak in 2017, eases in 2018–2019, rebounds in 2020, stays high in 2021, then plunges deeply negative in 2022–2023 before recovering sharply in 2024–2025.
- **Private nonguaranteed:** Flat and low in 2015–2016, jumps in 2017, declines but remains positive through 2021, turns negative in 2022–2024, and recovers to about zero in 2025.
- **Public and publicly guaranteed + IMF:** Climbs strongly from 2015 to 2018, dips in 2019, rebounds in 2020–2021, turns negative in 2022–2023, then improves to positive territory by 2024–2025.

**Source:** World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.  
**Note:** IMF = International Monetary Fund.
